articles.title: $50M EVO Entertainment Destination Breaks Ground in Downtown Clearwater
articles.summary: A major entertainment destination project is moving forward in Clearwater, Florida, with the site now cleared for a $50 million EVO Entertainment development. EVO Entertainment is a well-known multi-concept FEC operator combining bowling, cinema, gaming, and dining under one roof. This scale of investment signals continued confidence in the large-format FEC model in urban markets.

articles.title: accesso's Lee Cowie on AI, Data, and the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: accesso's leadership outlines how artificial intelligence and guest data are reshaping ticketing and in-park purchasing, with a clear goal of removing friction between guests and experiences. For FEC operators, the piece highlights practical steps toward seamless digital transactions and personalization. The shift from ticketing vendor to full guest-experience platform has significant implications for how FECs manage revenue and loyalty.

articles.title: InPark Magazine: Making the Guest Experience Frictionless Across Every Touchpoint
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's latest issue editorial focuses on removing operational friction throughout the guest journey, from ticketing to in-park spending. The theme is highly relevant to FEC operators looking to improve throughput and guest satisfaction without adding staff. Key contributors include accesso, Jora Vision, and others covering tech-enabled hospitality solutions.

articles.title: Texas' Largest Family Entertainment Center Set to Open in Houston in 2026
articles.summary: A new large-scale family entertainment center is slated to open in Houston in 2026, positioning itself as the biggest FEC in Texas. The project reflects continued investment in destination-style entertainment venues in major metro markets. FEC operators and investors should take note of how this venue's attraction mix and scale could shift competitive dynamics in the region.

articles.title: Jora Vision Expands Competitive Socializing Portfolio with New Interactive Game Concept
articles.summary: Jora Vision is broadening its offering in the competitive socializing space, developing new skill-based interactive game experiences designed for entertainment venues. The competitive socializing format continues to gain traction as an anchor attraction for FECs and adult-oriented leisure destinations. Operators looking to differentiate their attraction mix will find Jora Vision's evolving portfolio worth watching.

articles.title: 360Golf: Holovis Tech-Led Mini Golf System Brings Automated Scoring and Analytics to FECs
articles.summary: Holovis has developed 360Golf, a smart mini-golf system that uses individual smart balls and sensor-based scoring to eliminate manual scorekeeping and add gamified challenge elements. The system also provides operator analytics, making it a data-driven attraction option for FECs and leisure venues. Its competitive social gaming format and low-friction play experience align well with current FEC trends.

articles.title: Launch Family Fun Center Bringing Arcade and Trampoline Park to Pensacola
articles.summary: A new FEC called Launch is set to open on Davis Highway in Pensacola, combining arcade gaming with a trampoline park. The opening adds another active entertainment option to the Pensacola market and is part of a broader wave of trampoline and arcade hybrid venues expanding across mid-sized U.S. cities. Operators in similar markets should monitor pricing and attraction mix strategies.

articles.title: Six Flags and Warner Bros. Invest in Premium Interactive Horror with The Conjuring: Beyond Fear
articles.summary: Six Flags has partnered with Plague Productions and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences to create a premium interactive horror experience based on The Conjuring IP. The investment reflects a broader industry trend of charging premium prices for differentiated Halloween events that go beyond traditional haunted houses. FEC operators running seasonal scare events should study this model for upsell and IP licensing possibilities.

articles.title: Six Flags Fiesta Texas Breaks Ground on World's Longest Family Launch Coaster
articles.summary: Six Flags Fiesta Texas has broken ground on Werewolf Gorge, billed as the world's longest family launch coaster and the park's largest single-attraction investment ever, slated for a 2027 debut. The project underscores the continued appetite for record-breaking family-oriented thrill rides as a visitor growth driver. For FEC and regional park operators, the move signals that family coaster investments remain a high-priority competitive differentiator.

articles.title: Endless Surf and Flowstate Partner to Create AI-Powered Surf Park Technology Ecosystem
articles.summary: Endless Surf and Flowstate have announced a strategic partnership combining customizable wave technology with AI-powered computer vision to create a more connected operating platform for surf parks. The integration promises more personalized guest experiences and better operational data for surf park operators. As surf parks become a growing FEC-adjacent category, this tech partnership sets a benchmark for smart attraction management.

articles.title: Major Kansas City Entertainment Center Closes After 13 Years
articles.summary: A large entertainment center in Kansas City has permanently closed after 13 years of operation, drawing significant community attention. The closure highlights the ongoing challenges facing established FECs competing with newer, more experience-driven venues. Operators should examine what factors contributed to the closure as a cautionary case study in venue lifecycle management.

articles.title: Six Flags Darien Lake Drops Fright Fest, Shifts to Family-Friendly Halloween Programming
articles.summary: Six Flags Darien Lake has discontinued its Fright Fest event for 2026, replacing it with an expanded Oktoberfest and the family-friendly Kids Boo Fest daytime Halloween experience. The decision reflects a strategic repositioning toward broader family audiences rather than teen and adult scare-seekers. FEC operators planning fall programming should consider whether family-inclusive Halloween events can outperform traditional haunts for their demographics.

articles.title: Sky Zone Joins Toys 'R' Us and IKEA in North Suburban Chicago Mall Expansion
articles.summary: Sky Zone is among seven new tenants opening at a popular north suburban Chicago mall, joining major retail brands including Toys 'R' Us and IKEA. The placement signals continued FEC expansion into anchor mall positions as landlords seek entertainment tenants to drive foot traffic. This trend offers FEC operators and franchisors a compelling case for mall-based leasing strategies.

articles.title: India's Amusement Industry Sees Summer 2026 Growth Despite Rising Cost Pressures
articles.summary: India's amusement and entertainment sector experienced attendance growth in summer 2026, but operators are facing margin compression due to rising operational costs. The trend mirrors challenges faced by FEC operators globally, where post-pandemic demand recovery is being offset by inflation in labor, energy, and supplies. Operators in emerging markets should monitor cost-management strategies as a priority alongside growth planning.

articles.title: India's IAAPI Calls for GST Reform to Boost Amusement Industry Growth
articles.summary: The Indian Association of Amusement Parks and Industries is lobbying for GST rationalization to reduce the tax burden on the amusement sector and stimulate consumer demand. The advocacy effort highlights how tax policy directly shapes FEC profitability and accessibility in high-growth emerging markets. Operators and investors with international exposure should track this regulatory development.

articles.title: UAE Indoor Entertainment Boom Driven by Harry Potter, Disney, and Major IP Investments
articles.summary: The UAE is experiencing a surge in indoor entertainment development fueled by major IP-based attractions including Harry Potter and Disney concepts. The trend reflects strong consumer demand for premium, air-conditioned indoor experiences in the Gulf region's hot climate. FEC operators and investors should note that IP partnerships and climate-appropriate indoor formats are proving to be key growth drivers in this market.

articles.title: Indoor Entertainment Attractions Fuel UAE Leisure Boom
articles.summary: Indoor entertainment venues are playing a central role in the UAE's growing attractions market, with significant investment flowing into climate-controlled leisure concepts. The development aligns with broader Middle East trends of diversifying tourism through experiential entertainment. FEC operators looking at international expansion should consider the UAE as a high-opportunity market with strong consumer spending power.

articles.title: Mr. Putters Expands Indoor Mini Golf and Entertainment Offering Across Tampa Bay
articles.summary: Mr. Putters is expanding its indoor entertainment footprint throughout the Tampa Bay area, targeting families, schools, and corporate clients. The multi-segment approach to customer acquisition is a useful model for FEC operators looking to diversify revenue beyond walk-in guests. Group bookings from schools and businesses can provide a more stable revenue base for indoor venues.

articles.title: New Family Entertainment Center Opening in Rock Springs, Wyoming
articles.summary: A new FEC is set to open in Rock Springs, Wyoming, bringing structured family entertainment options to a market that has limited competition. Smaller market openings like this illustrate the continued geographic expansion of the FEC concept beyond major metro areas. Suppliers and franchisors should monitor Tier 3 and rural market opportunities as a growth avenue.

articles.title: Massachusetts Amusement Center Adds Four-Story Free-Fall Ride
articles.summary: A Massachusetts amusement center has installed a new four-story free-fall ride, adding a significant thrill attraction to its lineup. The addition demonstrates how established FECs are investing in marquee physical attractions to drive repeat visitation and social media buzz. Ride manufacturers and FEC operators should take note of how vertical thrill elements can reposition a venue's brand.

articles.title: Kaiqi Group: China's Leading FEC and Play Environment Manufacturer Goes Global
articles.summary: Kaiqi Group, founded in 1995 and headquartered in Shanghai and Wenzhou, has grown into a global supplier of integrated play environments for FECs, theme parks, and public destinations across 120 countries. The company's operations-first philosophy covers master planning through to post-installation operational support, making it a comprehensive partner rather than just an equipment vendor. FEC operators planning new builds or renovations should be aware of Kaiqi as a full-service international supplier.

articles.title: Alterface Marks 25 Years of Creating Interactive Themed Experiences
articles.summary: Alterface is celebrating 25 years of designing interactive dark rides and shooting experiences for themed entertainment venues worldwide. The company's technology underpins many successful interactive attractions that drive repeat visitation and guest engagement. FEC operators considering interactive dark ride or shooting gallery investments should evaluate Alterface's portfolio as a benchmark for quality and player engagement.

articles.title: Blue Sky Thinking in Attraction Design: How to Future-Proof Entertainment Concepts
articles.summary: Creative directors from Forrec and Moment Factory discussed blue sky design methodology at the Festival of Innovation, emphasizing that technology should serve storytelling rather than drive it. The panel offered practical guidance on designing attractions around timeless human motivators like curiosity and connection to ensure long-term relevance. FEC operators and designers can use these principles to stress-test new attraction concepts before committing capital.

articles.title: Urban Design Principles May Explain Why Some Attractions Outperform Similar Competitors
articles.summary: A blooloop analysis argues that urban design principles governing how guests move, orient, and make choices within a space may be the hidden differentiator between thriving and underperforming attractions. The piece challenges FEC designers and operators to think beyond storytelling and architecture and consider spatial flow and wayfinding as critical performance variables. Operators planning new venues or renovations should incorporate pedestrian movement analysis into their design process.

articles.title: Play Town Indoor Amusement Proposed for Milford, Connecticut
articles.summary: A new indoor amusement concept called Play Town has been proposed for a site in Milford, Connecticut, signaling continued interest in FEC development in the Northeast U.S. If approved, the venue would add structured family play options to a competitive Connecticut market. Local operators and regional suppliers should monitor the project's progress through the planning and permitting process.

articles.title: InPark Magazine Issue 111 Focuses on Frictionless Guest Experiences and Premium Halloween
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's 111th issue covers how technology is enabling frictionless guest journeys in attractions, with features on ticketing, in-park purchasing, and immersive Halloween events. Contributors include accesso, Jora Vision, and coverage of InfoComm 2026, making it a dense resource for FEC tech and ops leaders. Operators should read this issue for actionable insights on reducing guest friction and elevating seasonal programming.

articles.title: Tornado Terry's Family Amusement Center Turns to GoFundMe as a Last Resort
articles.summary: Tornado Terry's Family Amusement Center in the Fort Worth, Texas area has launched a GoFundMe campaign in an attempt to stay open, highlighting the financial vulnerability of small independent FEC operators. The situation serves as a cautionary reminder of the challenges facing owner-operated entertainment centers competing against well-capitalized regional chains. Industry associations and peer operators may wish to consider how community and industry support networks can help struggling small venues.

articles.title: Apex Entertainment Renews Partnership with New England Patriots' Andy Borregales
articles.summary: Apex Entertainment has renewed its community partnership with New England Patriots kicker Andy Borregales, linking the multi-concept FEC brand with a local NFL figure for marketing and charitable purposes. Sports athlete partnerships offer FEC operators a strong community visibility tool and can drive group event bookings and brand affinity. Operators looking to build local brand presence should consider similar sports or celebrity partnership models.

articles.title: NEAAPA Awards 2026 Pinnacle Scholarship to Funtown Splashtown Employee
articles.summary: The New England Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions has awarded its 2026 Pinnacle Scholarship to a rides department lead at Funtown Splashtown USA in Maine. The scholarship program recognizes frontline employees who demonstrate growth in guest engagement and leadership, supporting workforce development across the amusement industry. FEC operators should be aware of association scholarship programs as tools for staff retention and professional development.
